newsitem.title: BULGARIA: Bulgaria ends curb on dlr purchase for personal use.
newsitem.headline: Bulgaria ends curb on dlr purchase for personal use.

text.p: Bulgaria's cabinet on Thursday lifted a $2,000 annual limit on purchase of dollars for personal use on the domestic market following introduction of a currency board system.
"All restrictions for buying hard currency on the territory of Bulgaria have been lifted," Finance Minister Muravei Radev told reporters.
Foreign exchange export restrictions remain in force. Bulgarians still need a bank document to carry more than $1,000, when travelling abroad.
A previous ban, requiring that state firms buy hard currency only from banks, has also been lifted.
The central bank will continue setting foreign exchange rates based on the Frankfurt foreign exchange fixing, which will be used for accounting, statistical and customs purposes.
On Tuesday Bulgaria introduced a fixed exchange rate regime which requires levs in circulation be fully covered by foreign exchange reserves.
The lev is pegged at 1,000 to the German mark and the central bank guarantees to sell unlimited amounts of marks at that rate.
